data.name: Glorious Noon
data.detailed_description:
*THIS GAME IS STILL IN EARLY ACCESS DESPITE WHAT STEAM SAYS*


Looking for a fun way to exercise those virtual reality sword-fighting skills? Or perhaps you prefer to practice magic as well? From battling sky-pirates to taking down demon-elephant behemoths, Glorious Noon fulfills all of those needs by taking the player on a bombastic journey where he/she acquires enchanted weapons and the tenacity to use them. Along the way, discover magical artifacts to help fend off the terrifyingly beautiful monsters that roam this land.



List of Awesomeness
  • Stunning art and mythical beasts? Check.
  • Thrilling combat? Check.
  • Magic and mystery? Check.
  • All in virtual reality? CHECK!

Some Lore: Long ago, a daring warrior, a clever wizard, and an adventurous enchanter entwined their souls in an attempt to achieve immortality. Like all attempts to be immortalized, there was a curse attached: the three were caught in an endless cycle of rebirth and death. Only one of the three could be alive at a time so as soon as one of them died, the other sprang back to life.


You play as the warrior: a melee-based fighter who only uses weapons such as swords, spears, and crossbows. Depending on the enchantment on his/her weapon, the warrior can charge at an enemy at a high speed, pulverize the ground, and summon swords back to their hand.


Trailer Music: The Fat Rat Infinite Power
Music used in game: The Fat Rat Xenogenesis and The Fat Rat Unity

data.short_description: Hack and slash your way through hordes of fantastic monsters as you practice an engaging blend of magic and swordsmanship. Pulverize your enemies to pieces, dodge their sorcery, and gain aptitude over the weapons at your disposal. Arm yourself and use the environment in creative ways as you fight.

reviews.review:
Glorious Noon is a free-to-play virtual reality action game that embraces the fantasy of becoming a heavily armed warrior capable of cutting through strange creatures with both conventional weapons and supernatural abilities. Developed and published by Jehan Kobe Chang, the game originally released on November 14, 2017. Despite Steam presenting it as a released title, the store description specifically warns that the project should still be considered an Early Access game. That status provides useful context for the experience, since Glorious Noon has plenty of imaginative ideas but also carries the limited scope and unfinished qualities associated with an experimental independent VR project.

Combat is unquestionably the centerpiece. Glorious Noon is designed around physical VR interaction, putting swords, spears, and crossbows directly into the player's virtual hands. Rather than treating these weapons as interchangeable tools, the game supplements them with enchantments capable of dramatically changing how the warrior behaves in battle. Depending on the equipment being used, players can rapidly charge toward enemies, strike the ground with tremendous force, or summon thrown swords back into their hands. These powers give the fighting a playful supernatural quality and help distinguish the experience from a straightforward sword-fighting simulator.

The enemy selection supports the same exaggerated philosophy. Glorious Noon describes confrontations with everything from airborne pirates to enormous demonic elephant-like monsters, making it clear that realism is not the objective. Battles instead emphasize spectacle, movement, and improvisation. Players must attack creatures while avoiding hostile magic and finding opportunities to use their weapons and surroundings creatively. Because the game was built specifically around VR and tracked motion controllers, much of its appeal comes from physically performing attacks rather than simply pressing buttons and watching animations. Swinging a sword, handling a crossbow, dodging incoming sorcery, and recalling an enchanted weapon can create satisfying moments when the mechanics work together properly.

There is also a surprisingly interesting piece of mythology behind all the fighting. Long before the player's adventure, a warrior, wizard, and enchanter combined their souls while attempting to obtain immortality. Their plan succeeded only in the most unfortunate sense. A curse trapped the three characters in an endless cycle in which only one can remain alive at a time. When the living member dies, another returns to life. The player controls the warrior portion of this unusual trio, explaining the emphasis on physical weaponry while magical properties are largely delivered through enchanted equipment and artifacts.

It is a clever premise because it provides a narrative explanation for death and rebirth while leaving room for a much larger fantasy story. Unfortunately, Glorious Noon does not develop this concept as extensively as its premise deserves. The lore is more effective as background flavor than as the foundation of a substantial narrative campaign. There is enough mystery to make the world feel more interesting than a disconnected VR combat arena, but anyone expecting extensive characterization, elaborate storytelling, or a lengthy role-playing adventure should moderate those expectations.

Progression is instead closely tied to finding enchanted weapons and magical artifacts. Discovering new equipment expands the player's tactical possibilities, while repeated fighting encourages greater proficiency with the available arsenal. The combination of melee weapons, crossbows, enchantments, movement powers, environmental interaction, and magical artifacts gives players several different mechanics to experiment with. Glorious Noon works best when approached as a playground for discovering entertaining combinations rather than as a carefully balanced action RPG with extensive statistics and progression systems.

The visual direction complements this philosophy. Instead of pursuing strict realism, the game favors colorful fantasy environments and unusual mythical creatures. The result has an unmistakably independent character, but that modest production quality does not prevent individual monsters and combat situations from having personality. The developer's description repeatedly emphasizes mythical beasts, magic, mystery, and spectacular fighting, and the presentation generally supports that energetic identity. Its atmosphere is closer to a fantastical VR adventure playground than a dark or grounded medieval combat simulation.

Music adds another energetic layer to the experience. The game credits tracks by TheFatRat, including Xenogenesis and Unity for in-game music, while Infinite Power is credited for the trailer. These electronic compositions suit the deliberately bombastic tone and reinforce the sensation that Glorious Noon wants combat to feel exciting and theatrical rather than grimly realistic. English is supported for the interface, full audio, and subtitles. The game is single-player, requires VR, supports tracked controllers, and also includes Steam Workshop functionality.

The Early Access condition remains its largest drawback. Glorious Noon feels like the beginning of something potentially larger rather than a fully realized version of all its ideas. The reincarnation mythology could support a much deeper story, magical artifacts could form the basis of more elaborate progression, and the bizarre enemy designs could populate a significantly broader adventure. Players looking for the refinement, quantity of content, or consistency expected from a completed commercial VR action title may consequently find the experience rough around the edges.

Its free-to-play availability makes these shortcomings easier to accept. Glorious Noon is better viewed as an inventive VR experiment created around the pleasures of physical fantasy combat. There is genuine creativity in combining conventional medieval weaponry with enchanted movement, magical attacks, weapon recall, unusual monsters, and environmental interaction. The result may lack the depth and polish necessary to become a definitive VR action game, but it understands the immediate appeal of giving players extraordinary abilities and allowing them to physically act out the role of a supernatural warrior.

Ultimately, Glorious Noon is an ambitious but visibly unfinished VR adventure whose best qualities emerge from its imaginative combat mechanics. The strange lore, enchanted arsenal, mythical creatures, colorful presentation, and physically engaging fighting give it an identity of its own, even though its potential is greater than the amount of content ultimately realized. For players who already own compatible SteamVR equipment, its free entry point makes it an easy curiosity to explore, particularly for anyone who enjoys experimental sword fighting and magical combat. 

Rating: 7/10
